inline_comments.comment:
`serializeTagsParam` is typed `string` and returns `''` (not `null`/`undefined`) when both filter arrays are empty. The nullish-coalescing operator `??` only substitutes for `null`/`undefined`, so `'' ?? null` evaluates to `''`. Downstream, both `navigateTo` and `setQueryParams` filter with `v !== null && v !== undefined`, meaning an empty string passes through — the URL becomes `…&tags=` instead of having the `tags` param removed entirely. The PR description says clearing filters should remove the `tags` param from the URL; this is broken.

Fix: change `tagsValue ?? null` to `tagsValue || null`, or change `serializeTagsParam` to return `string | null` (returning `null` instead of `''` when both arrays are empty).

`storyPassesFilter` only matches entries with `type === 'story'`. When the user navigates directly to a docs URL (e.g., `/docs/my-component--docs`) with active tag filters, the entry in `filteredIndex` has `type === 'docs'`, so `storyPassesFilter` is always `false`. This causes an unconditional redirect away from the docs page even when the docs entry is present in `filteredIndex` and should be displayed.

Note that the `firstFiltered` lookup later in the same block correctly accepts both `'story'` and `'docs'` types, so the inconsistency is unintentional.

Fix: `const storyPassesFilter = filteredIndex != null && filteredIndex[storyId] != null;` (presence in `filteredIndex` is sufficient — the index already encodes filter results).

`state: { location } = {} as any` silences TypeScript with an `as any` cast to work around the fact that `location` may not be part of the module-args type. This suppresses all type-checking on the destructuring — if `state` changes shape, nothing will catch it here. Prefer either broadening the `ModuleFn` / module-args type to include `location`, or extracting `location` from `store.getState()` inside the function body (where the type is already known) rather than at the parameter level.

`navigateWithQueryParams` duplicates the URL construction logic (entries filter, sort, join with `&`) that already exists in `navigateTo` inside `url.ts`. Two copies of this logic must be kept in sync. Consider either exposing a `navigateToWithCurrentParams(path, options)` API method from the URL module, or composing navigation through `api.applyQueryParams` with an explicit path override. At minimum, extract the shared logic into a shared utility.

The `in` operator is used to check whether `includedTagFilters` / `excludedTagFilters` exist in the persisted object. Per project rules, `key in obj` can produce false positives from prototype-chain keys. Use `Object.hasOwn(persisted, 'includedTagFilters')` instead:

```ts
if (Object.hasOwn(persisted, 'includedTagFilters') || Object.hasOwn(persisted, 'excludedTagFilters')) {
```

The updated tests assert that `navigate` is called with the bare path (e.g., `'/story/a--1'`) and `undefined` as options. They only pass because the test's initial state has no `customQueryParams` (or they default to empty). There is no test that sets up active tag filters in `customQueryParams` and then verifies that `navigate` is called with the tags preserved in the URL (e.g., `'/story/a--1&tags=play'`). This leaves the primary new behavior — tags param preserved across story navigation — untested.

The existing test updates account for the double-read introduced by the migration loop, but there is no test that exercises the migration path itself — i.e., a case where `includedTagFilters` or `excludedTagFilters` exists in persisted storage and must be stripped. Without this, a regression in the migration code (e.g., the conditional never matching, or `set` not being called) would go undetected. Add a test case where the mocked storage contains stale tag filter keys and assert they are absent from the returned initial state.

general_comments.comment: `serializeTagsParam`'s declared return type is `string`, but the `persistFilters` caller treats `''` as a sentinel meaning 'no tags, remove the URL param'. This is a type-level mismatch: callers cannot distinguish 'no tags' from other empty strings, and the `?? null` pattern in the caller is incorrect as a result (see inline comment on line 453). A cleaner design is to change `serializeTagsParam`'s return type to `string | null`, return `null` (not `''`) when both arrays are empty, and update the caller to `return { tags: tagsValue }`. This makes the intent explicit and eliminates the need for a special-case coercion at the call site.

Test coverage for the new filter-aware initial story selection logic (the `hasActiveFilters && !stateHasSelection` block added to the canvas-route handler in `stories.ts`) is absent. The PR adds unit tests for `parseTagsParam`/`serializeTagsParam` and updates existing navigate assertions, but there are no tests that verify: (1) navigating to a URL with `?tags=play` auto-selects the first story that passes the filter; (2) navigating to a story URL that doesn't pass the active filter redirects to the first filtered story; (3) `selectFirstStory` with active filters selects from `filteredIndex`. These are the core behaviors of the PR and should be covered before merging.
